plan.stimulusBrief: An ORIGINAL English passage of 160 to 220 words (CEFR B1) about a small town that restored its old train station. Clear main idea, concrete details, one implied attitude or purpose, and one word whose meaning depends on context.

slots.focus: a detail stated in the passage
something the passage implies, or the writer's purpose
the main idea of the passage

stimulus.title: The Station Opens Again
stimulus.text:
For years, the old train station in Bellwater stood empty beside the market square. Its paint was peeling, and rain entered through holes in the roof. Some residents wanted to replace it with a car park, but a group of volunteers believed the building still had value.

With support from the town council, the group collected old photographs and spoke to former railway workers. They used these materials to repair the waiting room in its original colours. Local builders fixed the roof, while students made signs describing the station's history. The work took eighteen months and cost less than building a new community centre.

Last Saturday, Bellwater reopened the station as a public meeting place. It now contains a small library, a café run by a local family, and a room for music classes. During the opening event, visitors shared stories about journeys they had made from the station. The mayor said the project gave the town “a useful link to its past.” Although trains no longer stop there, the restored building has brought more people into the square and given residents a reason to feel proud.

items.stem: What did students do during the station restoration?

options.text: They made signs about the station's history.
options.rationale: The passage states that students made signs describing the station's history.

options.text: They repaired holes in the station roof.
options.rationale: Local builders fixed the roof, so this confuses the students' work with the builders' work.

options.text: They collected photographs from former workers.
options.rationale: The volunteer group collected photographs and spoke to former railway workers.

options.text: They served food in the new café.
options.rationale: The café is run by a local family after the reopening, not by students during restoration.

items.evidenceQuote: students made signs describing the station's history

items.stem: Why does the writer mention that the project cost less than a new community centre?

options.text: To show that restoration was a practical choice.
options.rationale: The cost comparison suggests that restoring the station was not just meaningful but also financially sensible.

options.text: To show that the town needed a larger library.
options.rationale: The passage mentions a small library but gives no reason to think residents needed a larger one.

options.text: To show that builders worked without payment.
options.rationale: A lower total cost does not mean that the builders were unpaid.

options.text: To show that trains would return to Bellwater.
options.rationale: The passage explains that trains no longer stop at the station.

items.evidenceQuote: The work took eighteen months and cost less than building a new community centre.

items.stem: Which statement best expresses the main idea of the passage?

options.text: Restoring an old station benefited the town in several ways.
options.rationale: The passage describes how the restored station preserved local history, created useful spaces, and encouraged town pride.

options.text: Replacing old buildings can improve a market square.
options.rationale: The town restored the building instead of replacing it with a car park.

options.text: Railway workers planned a new station for Bellwater.
options.rationale: Volunteers, the council, builders, and students supported restoration; former railway workers mainly shared information.

options.text: Music classes became the town's most popular activity.
options.rationale: Music classes are one use of the building, but the passage does not compare their popularity with other activities.

items.evidenceQuote: the restored building has brought more people into the square and given residents a reason to feel proud
